data.title: First Wireshark capture
data.what: Install Wireshark (macOS Arm), run ChmodBPF, capture Wi-Fi while visiting example.com. Filter dns, tcp.flags.syn==1, tls.handshake.type==1. Answer the 3 questions in notes/networking.md.
data.why: Every attack you'll ever detect moves over a network. Knowing what normal DNS, TCP and HTTPS look like is how analysts spot the abnormal.

data.title: TryHackMe: Pre Security path
data.what: Make a TryHackMe account. Do the Pre Security path in order: Intro to Cyber, Network Fundamentals, How the Web Works, Linux Fundamentals, Windows Fundamentals.
data.why: Structured basics of networks, web, Linux and Windows. Gives you a completion certificate and the vocabulary for interviews.

data.title: OverTheWire Bandit, levels 0–15
data.what: SSH into the Bandit server and clear levels 0–15. Log what command solved each level in notes/linux.md.
data.why: Security tools and servers run on Linux. SOC analysts live in the command line, and this is the fastest way to get fluent.

data.title: Put the portfolio on GitHub
data.what: Create or clean up your GitHub account, push the cyber-security repo, and add a profile README saying what you're learning.
data.why: This is the place employers actually see your work. Every later step adds evidence here.

data.title: Springpod cyber virtual work experience
data.what: Search Springpod for a cyber programme (e.g. Leonardo Cyber & Security) and complete it within its 2-week window.
data.why: Your first work-experience line for applications, plus a certificate. Can be done from home around school.

data.title: LinkedIn profile
data.what: Make a simple profile: A-levels, the cyber things you've done, and links to GitHub and certificates. Follow the employers on the Opportunities tab.
data.why: Recruiters check it. Following employers also means you see scheme openings early.

data.title: TryHackMe: Cyber Security 101 path
data.what: Upgrade to premium for a few months. Work through networking, Nmap, Wireshark, cryptography, Burp Suite and the defensive security rooms.
data.why: Moves you from basics to the actual tools used at work. It's also the base for SOC Level 1.

data.title: Apply for Year 12 work experience
data.what: Use the Opportunities tab: Uptree, Deloitte Career Shapers, HSBC, Leonardo, EY Foundation. Also ask your sixth form careers lead.
data.why: In-person work experience gives you real 'tell me about a time…' answers for apprenticeship interviews.

data.title: Apply for the CyberFirst / TechFirst summer course
data.what: CyberFirst is becoming TechFirst from Sept 2026, so check both names. Watch for the Year 12 summer course and apply the day it opens.
data.why: Run by part of GCHQ (the NCSC). One of the strongest things a Year 12 can put on a cyber application.

data.title: Build the home SOC lab
data.what: Install UTM. Create an Ubuntu Server VM running Wazuh, plus a victim VM with the Wazuh agent. Write down every step in lab/README.md.
data.why: This is your 'box'. It's real blue-team work, and building it proves skills that a course certificate can't.

data.title: Lab write-up #1: detecting SSH brute force
data.what: Inside the lab only: make repeated failed SSH logins, find the alerts in Wazuh, and write up what happened, how you saw it, and how to stop it.
data.why: A finished investigation you can walk an interviewer through. This is exactly what analysts do.

data.title: picoCTF competition
data.what: Enter picoCTF when it runs (usually in spring). Focus on the forensics and general-skills challenges.
data.why: A competition result on your CV, and good practice at problem-solving under time pressure.

data.title: Python project: log analyser
data.what: Write a Python script that reads an auth log, counts failed logins per IP, and flags anything suspicious. Put it on GitHub with a README.
data.why: Shows you can automate analysis. Scripting is what separates engineers from button-pushers, and it's more AI-proof.

data.title: TryHackMe: SOC Level 1 path
data.what: Work through phishing analysis, SIEM (Splunk/ELK), Sysmon, network security monitoring and digital forensics. Pause during exams.
data.why: The closest free-ish thing to SOC analyst job training, with a completion certificate.

data.title: End-of-Year-12 exams (cyber paused)
data.what: Cyber drops to zero. These results usually set the predicted grades on your applications.
data.why: Most apprenticeships filter on predicted grades first (e.g. JPMorgan asks for BBB including Maths).

data.title: Lab write-ups #2 and #3
data.what: Add Suricata and catch a port scan. Add Sysmon on a Windows VM and catch a suspicious PowerShell command. Write both up.
data.why: Three solid investigations make a real portfolio and give you plenty to talk about at interview.

data.title: First certification: CompTIA Security+
data.cost: Exam costs a few hundred pounds
data.what: Study with free Professor Messer videos plus practice tests, then book the exam. If money is tight, skip it: employers usually fund certs once you've started.
data.why: The certification UK cyber job adverts ask for most. It's a strong signal, but not required for apprenticeships.

data.title: Polish CV, GitHub and answers
data.what: Update your CV, pin your best repos, and draft answers to 'Why cyber?' and 'Tell me about a project' using your lab write-ups.
data.why: Makes applications fast and consistent when many open at once.

data.title: Apply to 6–10 degree apprenticeships
data.what: Apply the week each scheme opens (use the Opportunities tab). Many close early once they have enough candidates.
data.why: This is the goal: a paid job plus a free degree, starting Sept 2028.

data.title: Online tests and assessment centres
data.what: Practise numerical and situational judgement tests. Prepare to explain your lab work out loud in 2 minutes.
data.why: The final filter. People who can clearly explain things they've actually built get the offers.
